limitations: The web shell (`serve-http --ui`) is a diagnostic client of the HTTP binding: it edits nothing (Solve and Cancel are its only effects), calls seventeen operations and no other, computes only display arithmetic (design note §5.6), converts no unit, and judges nothing — the scenario view displays run differences without a registered comparison or allowance.

The web shell's security is the local, single-user model: loopback by default, the bearer token on every data request, a strict Content-Security-Policy; no TLS, no multi-user hosting, and no security assessment beyond design note §7. Served with `--allow-remote` over plain HTTP the page is an insecure context and record digests show "unchecked".

The web shell is tested in headless Chromium only. No usability, workflow or screen-reader study exists; accessibility is limited to status shown as glyph and word, controls that are keyboard-reachable by construction, and the measured contrast of its colour tokens.

The agent history shows what the project recorded, not what an agent claimed; the validation shown beside a commit is recomputed now by the current server, not the report the agent received at commit time.

W27's campaign (G16) is not run in M06: it is M07's (WO-17), after Frank's recorded spend approval and three real canaries; M06 commits the adaptation records only (provenance, access report, registration, coverage; R-175 to R-179), and no comparison with CRAFTS or OpenIDAES-450's reported results is made.

W26 and W27 are v0.2 requirement ids the manifest schema's `requirements` pattern ([DA]nn) cannot carry, and M06 maps to no D/A requirement (plan v1.2 §4.4, rows W26 and W27), so `requirements` is empty; the verdicts on W26 and W27 are the `verdict` lane's, not this manifest's.

Evidence class: software verification at C (tests, the gate, a local wheel install, the W27 dry run with stub sessions, and CI where recorded); nothing here is empirical validation or a usability study. Human numerical and process-modeling review remain `pending`; `reviewed` is never self-set.
